ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Kingdom OTSI sanctions list and New Zealand Sanctions Act 2023 designations. PEP screening is required for all directors, shareholders, UBOs and signatories; family members and close associates of PEPs are included. Enhanced due diligence is applied to clients from high-risk third countries. Screening results and supporting CDD records must be retained for at least five years under section 49 of the AML/CFT Act 2009 and reported directly to the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit where a match is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Company Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz/)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English or te reo Māori using Latin-alphabet characters. Non-Latin scripts, including Chinese characters, Cyrillic, Arabic or Devanagari, must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name or reserved name. The legal suffix 'Limited' or its approved abbreviation 'Ltd' must appear in the registered name. Punctuation is restricted to spaces, hyphens, ampersands, commas, full stops and slashes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 20 working days by filing an extension request with the New Zealand Companies Office before expiry. If the Companies Office refuses a proposed name, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 10 working days of the refusal decision, stating the grounds on which the name should be accepted and attaching any relevant ministerial or regulatory consents. The Registrar must issue a decision within 20 working days. If the reconsideration is unsuccessful, the applicant may appeal to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993 and the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable as the registered office address in New Zealand only where a licensed corporate service provider or natural person in New Zealand accepts service of process and maintains physical mail forwarding facilities. A P.O. Box may not be used as the registered office. The virtual office may also serve as the company's registered address for the purposes of the Companies Act 1993, provided the company maintains a verifiable remote-work address and a dedicated telephone/email contact for its remote screen-share and IoT software business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but not negligible. Based on the profile of a low-risk, remote-first software company with no physical inventory, the estimated annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by regulators is under 5%. This risk increases to approximately 15% if the company becomes the subject of an IRD tax audit, a police financial investigation or a formal AML/CFT compliance review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), principally sections 10-14 (incorporation, registration, and certificate of incorporation), 19-24 (company names and reservations), 26-36 (constitution and default rules), 65-69 (registered office and address for service), 84-95 (share register, director register, and officer appointments), 122-130 (written resolutions, share allotment and issue), 152-155 (director residence and disqualification), 190-199 (records and financial reporting), and 208-213 (annual returns). Subsidiary instruments: Companies (Fees) Regulations 2019; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 (private company exemptions); Income Tax Act 2007 and Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for tax registration; Tax Administration Act 1994 for IRD number administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies), a business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company — the online statutory incorporation application submitted through the New Zealand Companies Office 'Apply to Incorporate a Company' portal under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a New Zealand International Company. The Company may be incorporated without any paid-up capital and may allot shares of no par value for zero or nominal consideration under sections 124-130 of the Companies Act 1993. No escrow account, capital deposit, or banked-capital requirement is imposed by New Zealand law. The Company may be 100% non-resident-owned, provided that at least one director ordinarily resides in New Zealand or Australia (section 152, Companies Act 1993).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN THE MATTER of the Companies Act 1993 AND IN THE MATTER of [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company') — FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS dated [date], adopted at the inaugural directors' meeting held at [registered office address] or acting by unanimous written resolution under section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: (1) Constitution: that the constitution tabled at this meeting, or if no constitution is tabled, the statutory default rules contained in the Companies Act 1993, be and is hereby adopted as the constitution of the Company pursuant to sections 26-28. (2) Subscription and allotment of shares: that the incorporation subscribers subscribe for [ ] ordinary shares of no par value, and the directors are authorised to allot and issue such shares for a lawful consideration of NZ$[ ] per share (including nominal or nil consideration where lawful) in accordance with sections 128 and 129, and to enter each allottee in the share register under section 84. (3) Registered office: that the registered office of the Company in New Zealand be and is hereby fixed at [physical street address, New Zealand], and the directors shall cause any future change of registered office to be filed with the Registrar of Companies under section 67. (4) Officer appointments: that [name] be and is hereby appointed Chairperson of the Board, [name] Chief Executive Officer, and [name] Treasurer / Company Secretary (such latter office being optional), each appointment to take effect upon the execution of a written consent to act under section 87. (5) Tax and banking: that the directors be and are hereby authorised to apply to the Inland Revenue Department for an IRD number and, where applicable, GST registration; to open and operate corporate bank accounts; to engage Stripe and Paddle as merchant payment processors; and to execute all documents incidental to the Company's remote screen-share IoT software operations. (6) Statutory filings: that the directors shall cause the automatic NZBN allocation to be accepted, and shall ensure the filing of all annual returns (section 208), notices of change of directors or registered office, and other statutory lodgements. CERTIFIED as a true and correct record of the resolutions adopted by the Board on [date]. [Chairperson signature], [Company Secretary signature if appointed].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Availability Screening and Optional Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office — online Company Register name availability search and name reservation facility (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a pre-incorporation search of the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm that the proposed name is not identical to an existing registered name, is not reserved by another applicant, and is not objectionable or likely to mislead under sections 20, 21, and 22 of the Companies Act 1993 or the Fair Trading Act 1986. File an optional name reservation (valid for 20 working days) to ring-fence the name, and download the reservation confirmation for attachment to the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name (with alternative names if desired)
Written consent from any restricted-word authority (e.g., 'bank', 'trust', 'university') if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is declined as identical, reserved, or objectionable, immediately file an alternative name or apply in writing to the Registrar of Companies for reconsideration, supplying evidence such as letters of consent from prior name holders or trade mark coexistence agreements. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may pursue judicial review before the High Court of New Zealand.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / Te Tari Tāke — online portal: ir.govt.nz and myIR (secure customer portal)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident International Company in the CK_IC structure: (1) Confirm whether the company is resident or taxable in New Zealand; non-resident foreign companies without a fixed place of business or permanent establishment in New Zealand are not subject to income tax on foreign-source income. (2) If the company carries on business in New Zealand, it must be registered as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993 with the New Zealand Companies Office, which issues a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). (3) Apply for an IRD number through myIR or the applicable Inland Revenue registration form; foreign companies without New Zealand-source income are not statutorily required to obtain an IRD number, but if registration is needed for GST or withholding-tax purposes, the application must state the overseas registered office, certificate of incorporation (or equivalent), nature of services, and the specific New Zealand-facing activities. (4) For GST, submit the 'GST registration' application (registered person) together with IRD number application; a non-resident registered overseas company may allocate a GST return filing period (monthly / two-monthly / six-monthly) and must provide bank details for refunds through myIR.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' entity classification regime; corporate tax status is determined by statute. The relevant statutory mechanisms are: (a) a qualifying close-held company may elect to become a Look-Through Company (LTC) under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007, producing full tax-transparent treatment of income and losses; (b) qualifying affiliated companies may elect consolidated group treatment; (c) a non-resident International Company may rely on the territorial scope rules to maintain non-resident status if its central management and control is exercised outside New Zealand; (d) hybrid mismatch provisions (subpart FH of the Income Tax Act 2007) apply automatically and cannot be elected away. For the CK_IC non-resident International Company, no election is required to achieve tax-exempt foreign-source treatment absent New Zealand-source income or a permanent establishment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies (actual or expected) in any 12-month period; a non-resident supplier of remote services or low-value distributed digital goods into New Zealand must register only if its New Zealand consumer-facing supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no continuous transaction control system. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the PEPPOL standard through Inland Revenue's e-Invoicing service in myIR; GST is self-assessed on GST101 returns filed monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly via myIR, E-File, or gateway software. There is no API-based clearance mandate; however, registered businesses must retain electronically generated invoices and related records in a format capable of being accessed by IRD on request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For remote screen-share, unattended machine telemetry, and IoT remote-support software: zero-rating applies under section 11(1)(mb) of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the services are supplied to a non-resident person who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed. The supply must not be received by an individual physically present in New Zealand at the time of supply. Physical goods (e.g., IoT hardware, sensors, or screen-share appliances) are zero-rated only if they are exported by the supplier within 28 days of the supply to the non-resident recipient and are not subsequently returned or treated as supplied in New Zealand.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (NZ Customs Service electronic declaration through JADE and the Trade Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for physical IoT hardware / telemetry device exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank SWIFT / foreign-exchange records evidencing offshore proceeds)
Commercial Invoice and Software Supply / SaaS Agreement
Packing List (where accompanied by physical goods)
Certificate of Origin or technical-support evidence (where the overseas recipient's non-resident status is challenged by IRD)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may assess a shortfall penalty under Part 9 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. For fraudulent or intentionally misleading zero-rating claims, the penalty is up to 150% of the tax shortfall; an 'abusive tax position' attracts a 100% penalty, a 'gross carelessness' position 40%, and a 'not taking reasonable care' position 20%. Late payment and late filing penalties further accrue under section 139A, and use-of-money interest applies from the due date. Zero-rated export treatment is retrospectively clawed back if the exporter fails to substantiate exportation or the services were actually performed for a private consumer physically present in New Zealand; criminal prosecution is also available for tax evasion, false GST returns, and obstruction. The CK_IC structure must therefore retain contemporaneous IP geolocation, recipient residency certificates, bank routing evidence, and the underlying software delivery logs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua), operating in conjunction with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) and the Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) for AML/CFT supervision; New Zealand maintains a fully deregulated foreign exchange environment with no separate foreign exchange control authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is freely convertible on both the current account and the capital account. There are no exchange control approvals, surrender requirements, or investment licensing hurdles for software/IT service export revenues. Profit repatriation in the form of dividends is unrestricted, subject only to the Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) framework (statutory rate 15%, potentially reduced under an applicable Double Tax Agreement) and the standard company solvency test under the Companies Act 1993. Capital injections and outward capital redemptions are also unrestricted, though the bank will submit an International Transaction Reporting Form (ITRF) for Balance of Payments statistics. The only quantitative limitation is the aggregate risk-limit credit assessment applied by the commercial bank, not a regulatory restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender rules or mandatory conversion ratios in New Zealand. All exporters, including digital service providers, are permitted to retain 100% of foreign currency earnings indefinitely in onshore or offshore accounts. Receipts may be held in any freely convertible currency (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, NZD) and converted at commercial market rates at the discretion of the treasury function. The only administrative obligation is the statistical reporting of the underlying transaction via the bank's ITRF process when amounts exceed NZD 50,000 equivalent or when a payment crosses the border.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for ancillary payment collection lines; Low as the sole primary banking relationship. Wise NZ Limited is a registered bank and can provide a NZD account with strong cross-border rails, while Airwallex NZ Limited, Ebury NZ, and OFX are licensed Financial Service Providers and registered AML/CFT reporting entities under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008; however, they are not prudentially regulated as banks and cannot issue a settlement account for the target payment rails (Stripe, Paddle) without a deeper bank aggregate relationship. Legal constraints: any offshore digital EMI not incorporated or licensed in New Zealand is prohibited from holding client funds or providing a local NZD settlement account without a New Zealand AML/CFT registration and, if deposit-taking, a banking license. In practice, an International Company should open a primary corporate account with a tier-1 bank and use fintech EMIs only as sub-service treasury nodes for FX conversion and vendor payables.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned International Company operating remote software services, tier-1 New Zealand banks generally mandate an in-person KYC interview for at least one director or a designated authorized signatory who has physical presence in New Zealand. Fully remote account opening is not universally available; while some banks accept video-verified identity and apostilled corporate documents for low-risk SaaS entities, the practical requirement is typically a physical meeting at a New Zealand branch or a local introducer appointment (e.g., a registered New Zealand law firm or corporate services provider acting as a professional introducer). If no director can travel, the bank will require a New Zealand-resident agent director or an appointed local named signatory with full sign-off on account opening; otherwise, onboarding is deferred to a pre-approval conditional stage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt 'International Company' designation and non-resident beneficial ownership triggering enhanced due diligence under the AML/CFT Act 2009
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation; Memorandum and Articles of Association; Register of Directors, Shareholders, and Ultimate Beneficial Owners (UBOs) with passport copies; overseas government-issued certificate of good standing; entity structure chart demonstrating natural persons; legal opinion from a New Zealand-qualified practitioner confirming the entity's tax classification and the lawful basis for the tax-exempt status; personal source-of-wealth and source-of-funds declarations for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office located at a virtual office or corporate services provider address rather than a physical operational tenancy
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed registered-office service agreement with a licensed corporate secretarial provider; utility bill or lease agreement for any executive/engineering hub; explanation of the remote-first operational model; audited trail of revenue generation from the remote support software; confirmation letter from the external accountant that the registered address is standard market practice for the International Company.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity, multi-currency revenue aggregations received via Stripe and Paddle payout cycles from anonymous global end-customers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Stripe Connected Account Agreement and Paddle Merchant of Record Agreement; monthly payout settlement statements showing eindeutig correlation to SaaS license subscriptions; sample customer agreements and invoicing; transaction-volume forecast and explanation of refund/dispute patterns; implemented transaction monitoring and KYC for enterprise customers; documented IT security controls demonstrating low fraud/banking risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected inbound equity injection from an offshore parent shareholder into a newly-opened NZdraft capital account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving the share allotment and capital account opening; share subscription/application agreement; shareholder registry update under the Companies Act 1993; source-of-funds evidence from the investor's banking institution (six months of bank statements, tax returns, or a winding-up liquidity certificate); the investor's external legal confirmation that the funds are not proceeds of crime; a note explaining the business rationale for capitalizing a New Zealand entity for remote IoT/SaaS operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing protocol: (1) Execute a board and shareholder resolution to issue new shares to the non-resident parent/beneficial owner; (2) Complete the capital account opening form with the NZ tier-1 bank designating the account as 'Equity Capital – International Company'; (3) Instruct the sending bank to remit via SWIFT MT103 with payment field (Remittance Information) referencing 'Equity Contribution – Share Subscription NZ__NZ__CK_IC' and purpose code 'Equity Capital (S001)' or equivalent BOP code for Foreign Direct Investment; (4) where the transfer originates from a non-bank subsidiary or an individual, provide the source documentation above to satisfy CDD; (5) the receiving bank will complete an ITRF on the customer's behalf for RBNZ statistical purposes; (6) file the annual insolvency-solvency confirmation and maintain the register of shares. No exchange control approval or RBNZ license is required. For transfers exceeding NZD 1,000,000 equivalent, the bank may require additional positive credit evidence and a board-approved treasury policy.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for outbound disbursements: (a) SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for subscription royalties, cloud-infrastructure payments (AWS/Azure/GCP), affiliate commissions, contractor fees, and dividend distributions; (b) SWIFT MT202 COV for interbank cover payments where the ultimate beneficiary requires a clean bank transfer; (c) local NZD electronic clearing via Payments NZ (Bulk Electronic Clearing System) for domestic vendor dues in NZD; (d) Commercial Letters of Credit (documentary) are legally permissible but commercially irrelevant for remote software/telemetry licensing—such trade settlements are normally executed via corporate card (Stripe/Paddle payout settlement) or regular SWIFT transfers. For all outbound foreign-currency disbursements, the bank requires the invoice/contract as back-up and will flag the payment purpose as 'Software Licenses', 'Royalties', or 'Dividend' to comply with trade sanctions and anti-money laundering screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forward contracts with a New Zealand registered bank (tenors up to 12 months, with two-way margin support) used to hedge USD/EUR receivables into NZD for operating expenses
FX spot contracts executed through the tier-1 bank’s electronic dealing platform for immediate conversion of platform payouts (Stripe, Paddle)
Vanilla foreign currency options (call or put on USD/EUR vs NZD) for asymmetric protection of the annual revenue band
Cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating or fixed-fixed, NZD against USD/EUR) sized against intercompany loan principal and interest payments

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible under New Zealand law but are not market-standard for NZD because the NZD is a deliverable, freely floating currency; they may be considered only for legacy offshore books or where the counterparty lacks a NZD settlement account
Natural/economic hedging through holding a multi-currency bank account structure (USD and NZD accounts) and dollar-cost averaging conversions without a derivative instrument

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual return under section 214 of the Companies Act 1993
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 working days after the anniversary of incorporation; online filing may be submitted from 30 working days before the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZ$200 (approximately USD 128); continued non-compliance can trigger a default notice and eventual removal from the New Zealand Register, resulting in strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and auditor's report, if required under the Financial Reporting Act 2013
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If required, within 5 months after the company's balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver financial statements when required is an offence under the Companies Act 1993, with fines up to NZ$10,000; repeated non-compliance may lead to enforcement action and removal from the register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is required for a small non-reporting company. Audit is compulsory for FMC reporting entities such as listed issuers, banks, and insurers, and for large companies under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, generally those with total assets exceeding NZD 60 million or total revenue exceeding NZD 120 million.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS for Tier 1 for-profit entities; New Zealand IFRS with reduced disclosure regime for Tier 2 entities; small companies below the reporting thresholds are not required to prepare statutory GAAP financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently require a standalone public UBO annual filing for ordinary non-listed companies. The annual return confirms the directors and shareholders on record; shareholding transfers are recorded continuously in the Register of Members. The registered agent may require an annual private confirmation of the beneficial ownership chain for KYC and AML purposes, but no public declaration is filed with the Companies Office.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–700 for registered office and registered agent; USD 1,200–2,500 for full corporate secretarial maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000–18,000 if a statutory audit becomes required; not applicable below the audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand does not provide statutory tax holidays for general international companies. The R&D Tax Incentive provides a 15% tax credit (cash refundable) on eligible R&D expenditure, and the Approved Imputation Credit system attaches imputation credits to shareholder dividends to avoid double taxation. Loss attributing qualifying companies (LAQCs) and look-through companies (LTCs) provide flow-through treatment for eligible shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via myIR (Inland Revenue's secure online portal) or through approved tax software
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 7 months after the company's balance date if filed through a tax agent; otherwise standard filing date is 7 July following the balance date for a 31 March balance date. Provisional tax payments are due during the year (three installments based on prior year liability, standard uplift, or estimation) with final top-up due at the terminal tax date (generally 7 April following balance date).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income per financial statements (domestic and foreign-sourced income derived in New Zealand or attributed under controlled foreign company rules)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must report only New Zealand-sourced income and income attributed under CFC rules, with foreign-sourced income excluded unless specifically taxable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses, deductions, and allowances claimed against assessable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only to the extent they are incurred in deriving assessable New Zealand-sourced income and comply with apportionment rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income (assessable income less allowable deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents, calculate net New Zealand-sourced taxable income after applying any applicable exemption or limited income tax election

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses deducted (net losses carried forward from prior years applied against current-year net income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subject to shareholder continuity requirements (49% continuity for loss carry-forward) and available to non-resident companies that maintain required ownership continuity
Apply only verified loss balances; ensure loss continuity schedules are attached
Non-resident companies are taxed at the same 28% statutory rate on New Zealand-sourced income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Imputation credits attached to dividends received (if applicable for New Zealand-resident shareholder companies)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies generally cannot use imputation credits unless they are New Zealand residents; non-resident companies should disregard

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D tax credit claimed (15% of eligible R&D expenditure)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only for eligible New Zealand R&D activities performed in New Zealand; foreign-owned companies may claim for local R&D

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable (or refundable credit) after subtracting credits, resident withholding tax, non-resident withholding tax and provisional tax payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must reconcile any NRWT credits withheld on New Zealand-sourced income and terminal tax due

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach financial statements, tax reconciliation, and any required international tax schedules (e.g., CFC disclosures)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include required transfer pricing documentation and international questionnaire (IR1030 or equivalent, if applicable)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty commences at NZD 250 for late returns, plus NZD 50 for each further month (to a maximum of NZD 500 for late filing under the standard rules). Late payment: 1% initial penalty plus 4% incremental penalty per month (up to 8% maximum monthly); use-of-money interest (UOMI) is charged on underpaid provisional/terminal tax at a prescribed rate (currently approximately 6.78% per annum for underpayments). Additional penalties for knowingly providing false information may reach 150% of the deficient tax and lead to prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% for non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders, unless a reduced rate applies under a double tax agreement (typically 15% or lower for treaty jurisdictions).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must complete an IR290 (Certificate of Residence) from their tax authority and provide it to the New Zealand payer before payment. For Australian residents, an IR291 or equivalent Australian ATO (Residency Certificate) is accepted. The payer must hold a valid residence certificate at the time of payment to apply the reduced treaty rate; otherwise the 30% NRWT is withheld and a refund must be sought via an income tax return or IR67 claim. Inland Revenue also maintains an approved issuer levy (AIL) regime for certain inward interest payments.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 15% NRWT is the domestic rate for royalties paid to non-residents (withholding tax on royalties is subject to a final withholding tax under s 31, Income Tax Act 2007). Treaty rates vary, commonly 5% for certain industrial royalties (e.g., Australia: 5% in some cases; USA: 5% for certain property rentals). Interest: 15% NRWT domestic rate on interest paid to non-residents, but an Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% can be paid instead if the lender is a registered approved issuer and conditions are satisfied; treaty reduction may also apply. Interest paid to related non-resident lenders is subject to transfer pricing thin capitalisation (interest limitation) rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand does not prescribe a fixed local currency threshold requiring automatic Local File or Master File preparation; however, taxpayers must comply with transfer pricing documentation requirements based on the size and risk of cross-border related-party transactions. In practice, contemporaneous documentation is required for large multinational groups (typically consolidated group turnover exceeding NZD 500 million) with significant related-party dealings; smaller companies must maintain sufficient documentation proportionate to the complexity of cross-border transactions to demonstrate arm's-length compliance. Inland Revenue may request documentation for any transaction exceeding NZD 1 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Unspecified alternative methods may be used where they are materially more reliable and consistent with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand's substantive general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under s BG 1 Income Tax Act 2007 applies to void tax avoidance arrangements. For financial arrangements, the financial arrangements rules (s EW) require accrual-based spreading of income and expenditure. Although New Zealand does not have EU-style Economic Substance Regulations, the Inland Revenue applies a commercial substance test to determine residency, permanent establishment, and source of income of offshore companies managed from New Zealand. For an International Company (IC) structured as a non-resident entity, control and management exercised from New Zealand will create tax residency under New Zealand law, unless a DTA tie-breaker assigns residency elsewhere; thus a bare corporate structure without substantive activity in New Zealand or with management from New Zealand may trigger full New Zealand taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating New Zealand-sourced income, fabricating deductions, using sham offshore entities, or failing to disclose remote desktop support services rendered to New Zealand customers while claiming a captive structure in a tax-exempt zone with no economic substance or board oversight
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Administration Act 1994, a company is liable to a penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion or an abusive tax position, plus use-of-money interest. Criminal prosecution may result in fines up to NZD 50,000 per offense plus forfeiture of profits. Inland Revenue may also impose a civil penalty for not maintaining required tax documents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under the Tax Administration Act for tax withheld and not paid (e.g., RWT, NRWT, PAYE) under director penalty notices. Additionally, directors who participate in the use of a company to evade tax can be jointly and severally liable for the company's unpaid tax. Fraudulent conduct is punishable by imprisonment not exceeding 5 years. Courts may impose travel bans and asset freezing orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the 'Tax-Exempt Zone' international company status merely as a mailbox entity with no real business activity, no employees, no physical office, and no decision-making occurring in the jurisdiction of incorporation, while transacting with New Zealand remote-screen-share software customers through Stripe/Paddle and claiming foreign exclusion or no permanent establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may assess that the entity is a New Zealand tax resident because its central management and control is exercised in New Zealand, or that it has a permanent establishment in New Zealand through dependent agent or fixed place of business. The full 28% corporate tax applies to global income sourced from New Zealand and worldwide income if resident. Penalties for non-filing of an IR4 after assessment include daily penalties up to NZD 500 per month and UOMI. If the structure is a tax avoidance arrangement, the GAAR applies to void the arrangement and re-characterize the income, with penalty of 40% or 100% of the shortfall, depending on whether the dominant purpose is tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for tax shortfalls where they signed a tax return knowing it was false; penalties may be imposed on the officer under s 139B Tax Administration Act; for serious non-compliance, imprisonment up to 5 years for aiding and abetting tax evasion. Inland Revenue may also pursue personal recovery from directors for asset-stripped companies under the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Artificial TSM Attribution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underpricing or overpricing intra-group charges for remote desktop and IoT telemetry software licences, allocating excessive royalties to a low-tax jurisdiction, failing to submit contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, or creating circular fund flows between the International Company and a New Zealand subsidiary/agent using non-arm's-length margins attributable to an offshore treasury company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue can adjust the taxable income to reflect an arm's-length price under s GC 6 (transfer pricing). A documented shortfall penalty applies: 20% of the resulting tax shortfall if the transaction is deemed not at arm's length due to inaccurate documentation; 40% if there is an 'abusive tax position' and the taxpayer knew or ought to have known the pricing was not arm's length; up to 100% for evasion. Interest on underpaid tax compounds. Transfer pricing adjustment may also trigger NRWT withholding adjustments on any deemed dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors as 'controllers' of the company's pricing policy may be personally penalized if they actively participate in setting false transfer pricing documentation. In severe cases, criminal liability arises under 'dishonesty' provisions of the Crimes Act 1961 (obtaining pecuniary advantage), with imprisonment up to 7 years. Directors may also be liable for a culpable civil claim for restitution of any wrongful benefit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating remote desktop/IoT software without AML compliance where suspicious transactions are routed through payment facilitators (Stripe/Paddle) and structured to evade reporting obligations; accepting payments from sanctioned customers; failing to conduct customer due diligence where the entity falls within financial activity definitions (unlikely for pure software sales but relevant if the entity becomes a 'financial service provider' under the Financial Service Providers Act 2008 or if it provides payment/transfer services)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to NZD 250,000 for an individual and NZD 2 million for a company for each failure in the AML/CFT civil penalty regime; criminal penalties for a person who knowingly leaves proceeds of crime in an account may attract imprisonment up to 7 years. The Financial Markets Authority and Reserve Bank of New Zealand enforce the regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be prosecuted as 'senior managers' under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009; personal fines up to NZD 250,000 per offense and imprisonment up to 2 years for a senior manager who knowingly fails to report a suspicious transaction. A civil pecuniary penalty of up to NZD 2 million can be imposed on an individual, and the director may be disqualified from managing any financial service provider.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Appointing a nominee director with no actual authority or knowledge, failing to maintain a registered office, concealing the identity of the beneficial owner of the International Company from the Companies Office, or failing to file annual returns for the New Zealand registered foreign company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Companies Act 1993, the Registrar of Companies can deregister the company. Fines for failing to file an annual return: NZD 1,000 per month for a company, and NZD 500 for every director per month. Providing false information to the Registrar carries a fine up to NZD 10,000 per offense, and imprisonment up to 5 years for fraudulent filing. Inland Revenue can also access company and bank records under compulsory information powers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are knowingly parties to the carrying on of a business recklessly or fraudulently may be personally responsible for all debts and liabilities of the company under s 322 Companies Act 1993. In a tax context, directors who breach their duties may be exposed to a civil penalty of up to NZD 200,000 and disqualification, plus criminal restitution.
